spis.first_use.promise.title.en: Start from your existing reference corpus
spis.first_use.promise.title.for: walkthrough screen 1 title (its English is the screen's presentation in Sources/SpisDesktop/Resources/spis-desktop-first-use.json)

spis.first_use.promise.body.en: Spis starts from an evidence corpus you already maintain. It reads the original catalog, reference, provenance, screenshot, recording, and receipt files in place instead of copying a reduced collection.

spis.first_use.read_and_write.body.en: Choose an unpacked directory containing canonical example-catalogs.json, each catalog's sources.json and references.json, and all referenced record files. Spis validates the complete graph before saving the path. Archives are refused so no file or provenance field is silently omitted.
spis.first_use.read_and_write.body.for: walkthrough screen 2 body; keep the file names unchanged

spis.first_use.adopt_corpus.body.en: Choose your corpus directory. First use finishes only after Spis core accepts and persists the location and the app decodes a catalog from it. Repeated adoption reports the references unchanged rather than duplicating them.

walkthrough.eyebrow.for: small capitals label above the walkthrough; Spis is the product name

walkthrough.tagline.en: The measured state of the corpus, in one window
walkthrough.tagline.for: line under the label: what the app shows

walkthrough.step.for: badge: which walkthrough screen this is

walkthrough.continue.for: button to the next walkthrough screen

walkthrough.try_again.for: button that reloads a walkthrough that could not be read

walkthrough.unavailable.title.for: title when the bundled walkthrough could not be read

walkthrough.unavailable.body.en: The bundled walkthrough could not be read. Nothing in the corpus has been changed.
walkthrough.unavailable.body.for: body when the bundled walkthrough could not be read

walkthrough.fallback.body.en: Follow this step to reach the first catalog Spis can report on.
